en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Garlic Chapter 10.
The Training Rule on Dancing and Singing.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, there was a festival on the mountain peak in Rājagaha.
The group of six bhikkhunīs went to see the festival on the mountain peak.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
“How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whichever nun should go to see dancing, singing, or instrumental music, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means:
Whichever [nun] of whatever kind... [as before] ...a bhikkhunī...
[as before] ...this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Dancing" means any kind of dancing whatsoever.
"Singing" means...
Whatever singing there is.
"Instrumental music" means whatever instrumental music there is.
If she goes for the purpose of seeing, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Wherever she stands and sees or hears [him], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, having left the range of vision, she sees or hears him again and again, there is an offense of expiation.
If she goes to see one [nun] after another, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Wherever she stands and sees or hears [them], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, having left the range of sight, she sees or hears them again and again, there is an offense of expiation.
There is no offense if she sees or hears it while standing in the monastery;
or if, after she has arrived, they come to the place where the bhikkhunī is standing, sitting, or lying down, and dance, sing, or play instruments.
She sees or hears [it] while traveling along the path;
or she sees or hears it after going there because there is business to be done;
or in times of misfortune.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The first section: On Garlic.
